issues.where: data/public/dossiers/v2-astronomy-detector-erc-pi/prior_project.md WP2: 'magnitude 28 equivalent in the V-band, corresponding to 15 detected electrons per source'; '300-second exposure on an 8-meter telescope with 60% total system throughput'.
issues.problem: The new observing assumptions still do not support the brightness conversion. Using a standard approximate V zero point of 1.0×10^8 photons s^-1 m^-2 nm^-1, an 86 nm band, area π×4² m², 300 s and efficiency 0.60 gives about 491 electrons at V=28, roughly 33 times the stated 15. Fifteen electrons would instead require about 1.83% total throughput, a 9.17 s exposure, or V≈31.79 with the other assumptions fixed. A different narrow band or severe extra loss is not specified and cannot silently be folded into '60% total'. The 3.87 source-only SNR is consistent with 15 electrons, so simply replacing 15 with 491 would also change the simulated experiment.
issues.fix: Preserve the synthetic experiment without an unsupported on-sky sensitivity claim: replace the magnitude/conversion sentences with 'The simulations injected 10,000 artificial point sources with a Poisson mean of 15 detected electrons per source into empirical detector-noise backgrounds. No astronomical-magnitude or full telescope-sensitivity equivalence is claimed for this detector-only validation.' Delete the 300-second/8-meter/60% conversion and replace F07 with this detector-only limitation; retain 15 electrons and sqrt(15)≈3.87 as a source-shot-noise upper bound, not an on-sky SNR. State that sky background and a detector plate scale were not specified, so the reported recovery must not be extrapolated to real-sky completeness.
